title: Hair fall ad creative for Meta
gives: A grounded creative system for Arata: which ads to make, in what order, with finished copy and scripts for the hair fall core and the MitoActive launch.
live: Arata has a 40-concept creative portfolio live on Meta, Google and YouTube, every concept traced to a real review or claim, with a hook-level diagnostic running weekly and a monthly retro feeding the next slate.

blocks.text: Arata is the only brand in the ₹400 to ₹700 hair fall band that puts a study number on every bottle. 7.4X. 28,200. 95%. 86%. 87%. That is a creative asset most D2C haircare brands would pay a lot to own. Today it lives on the pack and on the product page. It does not yet run the ad account.

What we see in the brand's paid creative is a split personality. The culture work is strong: the Samay Raina mock podcast was built for recall, and the founders say so plainly. But recall ads do not sell a ₹571 serum to a 28-year-old in Bangalore who has already burned ₹3,000 on onion shampoo and biotin gummies. He needs a number, a timeline and a reason to believe. The brief tells us he is "sceptical from being burned by claims". The ad has to do the convincing before the landing page gets a chance.

The gap costs Arata in three places. First, MitoActive launched in August at ₹1,499 with zero reviews. A product with a new mechanism (mitochondrial function, Y100) needs education before it sells, and nothing in the current creative mix teaches it. Second, 68% of revenue sits on marketplaces and quick commerce, where Arata pays rent on every order. The ad account is the main lever to grow the 32% that runs through arata.in. Third, with ~650K monthly visits growing 42% month on month, creative fatigue is the next wall. A brand growing that fast burns through audiences and needs a creative pipeline, with a retro loop, rather than a campaign at a time.

The opportunity is simple to state. Arata has 2,248 on-site reviews and 2,435 Nykaa ratings full of verbatim customer language, six claims that are defensible, and two founders with a real origin story. That is a complete grounded inputs corpus. Most brands have to go and build one. Arata only has to use it.
This document gives Arata the creative strategy loop, the format portfolio, the hook matrix and the first month of finished assets.

blocks.text: Compliance guardrails for hair claims
Hair growth is a regulated claim space in India and a restricted one on Meta. Three rules apply to every concept in this document.

items: Every number carries its qualifier. "Up to 28,200 new hairs within 84 days" always includes "up to" and "84 days". "87% saw increased growth" includes "in 84 days". The words "regrow", "cure" and "100%" do not appear anywhere.

No before/after scalp photos in paid. Meta's personal health and appearance policy restricts imagery that implies unexpected results or triggers negative self-perception. We use text-based progression ("day 1 → day 84"), bottle counts and pillow shots. Crown close-ups and bald-patch zooms stay out.

Advertising standards complaints against hair growth ads are upheld often. We keep the study design one tap away (Lab Notes explainer) and mirror the pack language exactly, so the ad never claims more than the bottle does.

Example 5: WhatsApp chat reveal (Lane A warm, T2)

The iMessage reveal format, built on the surface Indian customers actually use. 9:16, WhatsApp dark theme in a phone frame over a bathroom-shelf photo. 11 bubbles, about 19 seconds, then a 3-second static end card. Dramatized conversation, labelled "Sponsored" by placement. The brand appears once, late.

[Aman]      pillow is clean in the morning. that's all i wanted

[Aman]      arata. hair growth intensive serum. the pack of 3
[Karan]     ordering

**End card:** Hair Growth Intensive Serum, Pack of 3, ₹999. "Up to 28,200 new hairs within 84 days, in a consumer study." Logo SVG, static, no drift.

**Pacing:** reactions 300 to 400ms apart, sentence replies get 700ms of air, typing indicator (silent) before "pillow is clean" and before "arata.". 600ms of silence before "ordering". WhatsApp send and receive tones, music bed at 30% with a fade before the brand bubble.

**Grounded in:** Pack of 3 price and claim from the catalogue. "Pillow is clean" dramatizes the review theme "hair fall reduced drastically" and the JTBD "stop the hair fall I see on the pillow". No real customer is named. If Arata approves a code (assumption: ARATA84), it goes inside the "arata." bubble, link-underlined, and on the end card.
Example 6: FAQ card set (B-tier, Lane B warm, four statics)
Each card: the objection in the customer's words at the top (60% of frame), the answer in two lines, the bottle small at the bottom. Lab-blue type on white.
**Card 1** **Q:** "₹1,499 for 30 ml is a lot." **A:** It is one month, twice a day. ₹50 a day. A diagnosis kit runs ₹1,400 to ₹1,800 a month for five months.
**Card 2** **Q:** "Is this just another Redensyl serum?" **A:** Those work on the follicle. Y100 works on the mitochondria that power it. Licensed exclusively to Arata in India.
**Card 3** **Q:** "Do I have to use it forever?" **A:** A 3-month course, then maintenance. Minoxidil is a dependency. This is a plan with an end date.
**Card 4** **Q:** "What if the bottle leaks?" **A:** Replaced, no questions. Reply to your order message and a new one ships.

**Grounded in:** The objections table in the brief, verbatim. Card 4 depends on Arata confirming the replacement promise (listed as an operations fix in the brief). It does not run until the policy is live.

blocks.text: **Decision rules**

items: No verdict before 1,000 impressions per concept. A two-day read is a coin flip.
Judge concepts, not ads. Three executions of "84 days, one number" failing means the concept is wrong. One failing means the execution was.
A full-funnel loser with one strong metric is a lead. It goes back to the icebox as an iteration, with the weak stage named.
If Lane A winners hold for 30 days: shift to 60% winner-led variations, keep 15% exploration alive, raise Lane A budget share by 10 points.
If Lane B shows no single-metric hit in 30 days: the VSL mechanism framing is wrong, so we test the price-math hook and the upgrade-from-Intensive-Serum hook before touching production budget again.
If rolling reach drops two weeks in a row: deploy the next creator partnership ad before adding any more statics.
If CTR is strong and CVR is weak on any concept: fix the landing page before iterating the ad.
